blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
British culture has a few rules. Nobody writes them down, but everybody follows them. If you break one, people notice at once.

The most important rule is the queue. In the UK, you must wait for your turn. You stand in line, you wait, and you do not push. The queue is a matter of honour.

Today we practise must and should. "Must" is a rule you have to follow. "Should" is friendly advice. You must queue. You should say "thank you". Manners are a quiet language, and watching people is the fastest way to learn.

items.q: What does the text say about British rules?
options: Nobody writes them down, but everybody follows them.
They are written on signs everywhere.
items.why: "Nobody writes them down, but everybody follows them."

items.q: What is the most important rule in the text?
items.why: "The most important rule is the queue."

items.q: What is the difference between "must" and "should"?
options: "Must" is for the past; "should" is for the future.
"Must" is a rule; "should" is friendly advice.
items.why: "'Must' is a rule you have to follow. 'Should' is friendly advice."

items.q: The text suggests that if you push in a queue, people will most likely…
options: notice and think it is rude.
items.why: Inferência: "If you break one, people notice at once" e a fila é "a matter of honour".

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: watching people helps you learn the rules.
you should push to be faster.
you must talk loudly in public.
items.why: Inferência: "watching people is the fastest way to learn."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie falar com um visitante. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hello! Welcome to London. It is your first day here, so let me help you with a few small things.

First, the queue. Look — all these people are waiting in a line for the bus. This is very important in the UK. You must wait for your turn. You do not push, and you do not go to the front. If you push in front of people, everyone will look at you. It is not polite, and here it is a big mistake.

Second, say "thank you". You should say it a lot. Thank you to the bus driver, thank you to the person in the shop, thank you to everyone. It is very normal here, and people like it.

On the Tube, the train under the city, you must be quiet. You mustn't talk loudly on the phone. People are tired after work, and they like a calm, quiet trip home.

And one more thing: you should hold the door for the person behind you. It is a small thing, but it is very nice.

Do not worry about all these rules. Just watch other people and do the same. That is the best way to learn. In one week, you will feel like a real Londoner!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie say about the queue?
options: You must wait for your turn.
You can go to the front.
items.why: "You must wait for your turn. You do not push."

items.q: What should you say a lot, according to Sophie?
items.why: "You should say it a lot. Thank you to the bus driver..."

items.q: What is the rule on the Tube?
items.why: "On the Tube... you must be quiet. You mustn't talk loudly on the phone."

items.q: Sophie's advice suggests that the best way to learn the rules is to…
options: watch other people and do the same.
items.why: Inferência: "Just watch other people and do the same. That is the best way."

items.q: How would you describe Sophie's tone?
items.why: Inferência: ela diz "Do not worry" e ajuda com um sorriso — é gentil, não dura.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "There is a long queue at the coffee shop." A queue is…
items.why: Queue = fila: uma linha de pessoas esperando.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please ___ here. Your table will be ready in five minutes."
items.why: Wait = esperar; é o que se faz na fila.

items.q: "It is a rule: you must show your ticket." A rule is…
items.why: Rule = regra: algo que você deve seguir.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We show ___ when we say thank you and hold the door."
items.why: Respect = respeito: mostramos respeito com boas maneiras.

items.q: "Please wait for your turn." Your turn is…
options: the moment when it is your time to go.
items.why: Turn = vez: o momento em que chega a sua hora.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns no dia a dia. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Please line up at the door." To line up means to…
options: form a queue, one behind the other.
items.why: Line up = formar fila, um atrás do outro.

items.q: "Can you hold the door for me?" This means…
options: keep the door open for the next person.
items.why: Hold the door = segurar a porta aberta para a próxima pessoa.

items.q: "Sorry, you cut in line." To cut in line means to…
options: go in front of others without waiting.
items.why: Cut in line = furar a fila, passar na frente sem esperar.

items.q: "Please keep quiet on the train." To keep quiet means to…
items.why: Keep quiet = ficar em silêncio, não fazer barulho.

items.q: "It's your turn — please go ahead." To go ahead means to…
items.why: Go ahead = pode ir, siga em frente / prossiga agora.
